claims.text: Machine-learning models trained on high-throughput density-functional-theory calculations and experimental data can accurately predict thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys in high-temperature solid and liquid states.
Atomic arrangement and bonding are the structural mediator relevant to the proposed intervention.
Machine-learning models learn patterns from density-functional-theory calculations and experimental data.
Learning these patterns enables prediction of high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties.
The intervention will improve accuracy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve the availability of thermodynamic-property determinations relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve the efficiency of thermodynamic-property determinations relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The predicted properties include melting temperature, enthalpy of fusion, entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties.
The proposed approach is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing 5–10 principal elements.
The proposed approach is applicable between 500 and 2000 K.
Limited availability of high-quality training data may constrain the proposed approach.
Biases in machine-learning models may constrain the proposed approach.
Deviation of more than 10% from independent experimental data and computational simulations is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
